title: A fixed 51.56-day wave reduces pooled held-out error in eight HD 40307 HARPS seasons
abstract: We test seasonal transfer of the known 51.56-day velocity signal of HD 40307. We use 448 selected HARPS RVBank Ver.02 exposures on 232 nights. Eight held-out seasons contain 211 nights. A common wave fitted to the other seasons reduces pooled held-out weighted error by 13.8 percent in SERVAL and 7.0 percent in DRS. Local nuisance terms are refitted in each held-out season. Six of eight SERVAL seasons and four of eight DRS seasons give positive gains. Seasonal phase and amplitude changes give no clear improvement in conditional residual-sign tests, with or without a period search. Power against 0.8 m/s random seasonal phases ranges from 54 to 95 percent under the tested residual models, so the null does not establish fixed phase. The two reductions use the same spectra. We find no new planet or independent confirmation. Code, aggregate results, input hashes, a figure and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Fixed-wave transfer varies by season. Conditional tests give no clear evidence of seasonal changes, but this does not prove a stable orbit.

citations.reason: Its alias study leaves seasonal phase coherence open. We reuse the identified public input, not its code.
Includes a short two-epoch control at this period. We add eight-season transfer and seasonal-change tests.
